findings.claim: The new bullet tells OpenCode workers to put their `## Key Learnings` block at the end of their report. The plugin cuts the text it sends to `memorycard capture` to 256 KiB and keeps the start (memorycard-opencode-plugin.mjs:119-126: `bytes.subarray(0, end)`). So when a subagent's final text is longer than 256 KiB, the block this rule asks for is the part that gets cut, and nothing is captured; the only trace is the 'capture input truncated' log line. The truncation code was not changed; this commit makes it matter. A final reply this long is unlikely. Possible fixes: keep the tail when cutting, or keep the trailing Key Learnings section.

The banned list gained `subagent-stop` and `orchestrator`, but the failure message still says each banned word is 'not a memorycard tool'. Neither word is a tool: one is Claude Code's hook and the other is the retired gentle-ai rule. If either word comes back, the failure will misdescribe what was found and why it is banned.

evidence: Read T61 (line 103), L163, L166, the S13 L166 amendment and L167 (owner's approval of the exact R1 bullet).
